questions.title: The sugar type that determines ABO antigen specificity
questions.question: What is the primary type of carbohydrate molecules that determine the ABO blood group antigens on the red blood cell surface?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Disaccharides (two linked sugar units, like lactose or sucrose) are not what determines ABO antigen specificity.
explanations.B: Correct. While the ABO antigen as a whole is a branched oligosaccharide chain, blood-group specificity is set by which single further monosaccharide a person's own glycosyltransferase adds onto the shared H-antigen core: an extra N-acetylgalactosamine gives the A antigen, an extra galactose gives the B antigen, and no further addition leaves the O phenotype. So the primary carbohydrate TYPE that determines specificity — the one differing residue a transferase enzyme adds — is a monosaccharide.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Polysaccharides are long chains of many repeating monosaccharide units (like glycogen or starch), a different scale of molecule from the single terminal sugar that sets ABO specificity.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Glycogen is the body's storage polysaccharide of glucose, unrelated to red-cell surface antigen specificity.

questions.learning_objective: State that a single terminal monosaccharide determines ABO antigen specificity.
questions.source_citation: FOMSCU Foundation 1 Formative and Past Exams 2021, Q3 (also Formative 2023 Q3)
